newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU set to press Hashimoto on U.S. bonds warning.
newsitem.headline: EU set to press Hashimoto on U.S. bonds warning.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto began talks with his Dutch counterpart Wim Kok on Wednesday ahead of a summit with the European Union which is expected to be dominated by trade and investment.

Hashimoto, who arrived in the Netherlands on Tuesday night, viewed a guard of honour at The Hague's historic Binnenhof, home of the parliament, before begining brief talks with Kok on bilateral relations.

Kok, who is currently also president of the EU under the 15-nation bloc's six-month rotating system, was later to be joined by European Commission President Jacques Santer and trade commissioner Sir Leon Brittan for the annual EU-Japan summit.
EU officials are likely to want to press Hashimoto to expand on his comments made on Monday regarding Tokyo's huge holdings in U.S. treasuries which sent financial markets into a spin.

During a visit to the U.S., Hashimoto said in the past Japan had been tempted to sell some of its treasuries but had not done so. "I hope the U.S. will engage in efforts and in cooperation to maintain exchange stability so we will not succumb to the temptation ... and switch to gold," he said.
Japanese officials have since sought to play down his comments, but some analysts have read his message as a thinly-veiled warning to Washington not to press Tokyo too hard over its trade surplus.

EU officials will take the opportunity on Wednesday to brief Hashimoto on the economic and monetary union situation as well as membership of the Korean Energy Development Organisation, the group set up to press North Korea to focus its nuclear aspirations on energy and not weapons.
They will also discuss global environmental issues, the international fight against drug trafficking and terrorism and African development.
